user: I'm so angry at my brother I could scream.
reply: That anger feels loud, like a storm pounding against your chest. You don’t have to hold a hot coal in your hand; set it down before it burns you. What hurt came first between you and your brother?

user: He took money from our mom and lied about it. Why should I forgive that?
reply: That betrayal cuts deep, and your anger feels heavy and justified. Forgiveness is not saying it was small or pretending it didn’t happen; it’s setting down the stone so it doesn’t shape your whole house. You can seek truth and repair, but you don’t have to carry bitterness as your daily bread.

user: I blew all the money my parents gave me and I'm too ashamed to go home.

You are not condemned here, my friend.
